newsitem.title: UK: World wheat stocks to stay tight.
newsitem.headline: World wheat stocks to stay tight.

text.p: Global wheat stocks are likely to remain tight despite higher production, a leading international authority predicted Thursday,
The London-based International Grains Council forecast that an increase in wheat production would be soaked up by greater usage in 1997-98.
The IGC predicted a rise in world wheat output to 583 million metric tons this year, from 1996's 579.5 million tons.
But it also forecast world wheat usage to rise to 582 million tons from 556 million tons, leaving little chance to rebuild stocks.
With governments less willing to hold wheat -- as seen in the now tiny size of the once notorious European Union "Grain Mountain" -- the onus is on a constant flow of supply.
"Production is all-important now that we don't have a large volume of carryover," the council's Bill De Maria told Reuters.
The IGC forecast carryover stocks to stay at 100 million tons, unchanged from 1996-97, and vastly reduced from previous years.

The crux of the problem stems from China, where the IGC forecast an increase in imports to 7 million tons from 4 million previously, to be matched by a 2-million ton increase in use, to 120 million tons.
Increased demand in Far East Asia and from a rapidly expanding population in India were also key to the forecast uptrend in consumption.
The IGC also saw increased wheat usage in the Former Soviet Union and Eastern Europe as demand for animal feed recovers from a dip over several years amid the upheavals in the region.
Low reserves make trade an essential element in smoothing out the ups and downs of supply and demand, De Maria said.
